summary: Same pattern — wandering point 'flies' on a strip, each trailing a fading comet tail in a fixed 4-colour palette — but the port draws ~1.75x too many flies, moves them ~1.8x too slowly, and badly mis-weights the colour mix (original is ~95% red+green with rare gold/azure accents; port is only ~24% green with orange+blue at 5x their proper share), so the original reads as a Christmas string while the port reads as a generic multicolour one.
observations: Rig: strip, 60 px, no controls on EITHER side (probe: 'no settable controls' for orig and port) — control surfaces match exactly.

Both sides render, compile clean, and are alive and steady over 240 s (survey-240) and 60 s at 20 fps (long20): orig meanBrightness swings 11-49, port 23-50, neither decays, freezes or saturates. brightnessTrend 'decaying' in the 6 s baseline is just envelope noise, not a dying port.

Structure (matching): both draw isolated bright fly heads that wander back and forth along the strip, each leaving a fading tail behind it; both dwell for several frames at the strip ends before turning around (endpoint pixel at full brightness in 49/240 orig vs 53/240 port frames over the 6 s baseline) — no wall-pinning asymmetry.

PALETTE VALUES: both sides use exactly 4 fixed colours (hue histogram of >200-brightness pixels over 120 frames shows 4 clusters per side). orig = red (255,0,0 / h0.000), orange (255,152,0 / h0.100), green (51,255,0 / h0.300), azure (0,102,255 / h0.600). port = red (255,0,0 / h0.000), orange (255,137,0 / h0.090), green (5,255,0 / h0.333), blue (0,10,255 / h0.660). The port's green is pure-green instead of the family's signature yellow-green 51,255,0, and its blue is a deep royal blue instead of the original's azure/sky blue.

COLOUR MIX (headline divergence): census of every fly at t=0 on a 300 px rig over seeds 1, 7 and 1234 — orig 78 flies total: red 46%, green 49%, orange 3%, blue 3%. port 136 flies total: red 47%, green 24%, orange 15%, blue 15%. The port halves green's share and gives orange and blue about 5x their proper weight. Weighting by lit pixels over a 6 s window agrees: orig green 47% / red 29% / orange 14% / blue 8%; port red 32% / orange 30% / blue 22% / green 17%.

The colour-mix gap is obvious to the eye: at seed 1234 the original's 6 s waterfall is dominated by broad green arcs with red and one gold arc, while the port's is dominated by red and blue zigzags with only two green traces. In the late window (--skip 40) the original is green+red and the port is orange-dominated.

FLY COUNT: port draws ~1.75x too many. t=0 census, 300 px, 3 seeds: orig 26 flies per 300 px, port 45. On the default 60 px rig at t=0: orig 6/7/6 flies (seeds 1/7/1234), port 9/12/12. Count scales with pixel count on both sides (same law), so this is a density constant, not a rig artefact. Corroborated over time: full-brightness head count sampled across the 6 s baseline is 80 (orig) vs 144 (port).

FLY SPEED: port's flies move ~1.8x too slowly. Head-tracking on the default 60 px rig over 6 s: orig mean |velocity| 6.3 px/s, port 3.4 px/s. On 300 px: orig 8.6 px/s, port 4.5 px/s, median PEAK speed per track orig 14.0 px/s vs port 8.0 px/s. Travel range over 6 s on 60 px: orig up to 32 px (over half the strip), port max 13 px — the port's flies stay stuck in a small neighbourhood.

MOTION CHARACTER (matching): both are drift-with-easing, not ballistic-with-bounce. Fraction of a track's time spent below 25% of its own peak speed: orig 0.140, port 0.171; direction reversals 0.30/s vs 0.28/s. Tracked paths on both sides show smooth acceleration, multi-frame dwells at turnaround, and mid-strip reversals. (The 'orig curves, port zigzags' impression from the waterfalls is a trail-width artefact — it does not survive per-frame position tracking.)

TRAIL SHAPE: the original's tail is longer and ramps smoothly; the port's is shorter and drops off abruptly. Median lit extent (>=30/255) around a full-brightness head: orig 9 px vs port 6.6 px at 60 px (8.4 vs 6.7 at 300 px). Profile at 60 px, orig: 11,57 -> 99 -> 144 -> 209 -> 255,255,255,255 (a smooth ~8 px ramp into the head). Port: 255 -> 111 -> 63 -> 58 -> 18 -> long dim floor near 10 (halves within 2 px, then a faint plateau).

FPS coupling: both sides behave the same way. Whole-frame decorrelation to corr=0.5 takes orig 7.2/6.0/9.2 frames and port 7.9/7.6/12.4 frames at 10/20/40 fps (0.72/0.30/0.23 s vs 0.79/0.38/0.31 s) — both are roughly frame-stepped, and the port is consistently ~1.25x slower to decorrelate at every rate. No frame-rate-coupling divergence between the sides.

Long-term rhythm: no modes, no regimes, no periodicity. Autocorrelation of meanBrightness over 1200 frames at 20 fps shows monotonic decay with no peak on either side; the 240 s / 2 fps survey and the 60 s / 20 fps run are one continuous regime on both sides. The two sides' 1 s-binned brightness envelopes over 60 s correlate at r=0.54 (shared slow spawn/decay rhythm), with the original swinging harder (11-49 vs 23-50).

Overall level: port is slightly brighter/denser (baseline mean 37 vs 30; long20 mean 36 vs 31), a direct consequence of the extra flies; motion stat orig 6.1 vs port 4.8 avg, consistent with the slower flies.
Seed-independence checked at seeds 1, 7 and 1234: every finding above (count, speed, colour mix, palette values) reproduces on all three.
feedback: Colour weighting is the biggest visible miss. The original picks a fly's colour from 4 slots with a heavily skewed distribution: red ~46%, green ~49%, gold/orange ~3%, azure ~3%. The port is picking red ~47%, green ~24%, orange ~15%, blue ~15%. Cut orange and blue to roughly 1-in-30 rare accents each and give the freed share to green, so the strip reads red-and-green with an occasional gold or blue fly.

Fix the exact palette constants. The original's green is RGB(51,255,0) — hue 0.30, a yellow-green, the same signature green other Christmas-family patterns in this corpus use — not hue 1/3 pure green (5,255,0). Its blue is RGB(0,102,255) — hue 0.60, a sky/azure blue — not hue 0.66 royal blue (0,10,255). Its orange is RGB(255,152,0) — hue 0.10 — not hue 0.09 (255,137,0). Red (255,0,0) is already correct.

Fly population is ~1.75x too dense. On the default 60 px strip the original has 6-7 flies; the port has 9-12. On 300 px the original has ~26 and the port ~45. The scaling law (flies proportional to pixel count) is already right — just scale the constant down by ~0.57.

Flies fly ~1.8x too slowly. On the 60 px default rig the original's flies average 6.3 px/s of travel and peak near 14 px/s on a 300 px rig; the port averages 3.4 px/s and peaks near 8 px/s. Consequence: over a 6 s window an original fly can traverse 32 px (half the strip) while the port's never leave a 13 px neighbourhood, so the port looks like it is hovering. Roughly double the per-frame step; the easing/turnaround character is already correct and should be preserved.

Tail rendering: the original's comet tail ramps smoothly from near-zero up to the head over about 8 px (values like 11 -> 57 -> 99 -> 144 -> 209 -> 255), giving each fly a soft feathered streak. The port's tail halves within 2 px of the head and then sits on a long dim floor around 10/255, so its flies read as hard dots with a faint smear. Lengthen the bright part of the tail and drop the residual floor. Note that doubling the fly speed (above) will lengthen the tail on its own if the decay is time-based — retune the tail only after the speed fix.

Everything else is right and should not be touched: no controls on either side, wandering-with-easing motion (including multi-frame dwells at the strip ends and mid-strip reversals), the frame-stepped timing character, and the slow shared spawn/decay brightness envelope.
